Feature-rich

Everything a WebSocket app needs, on both sides.

  • WebSocket Server

    Behind net/http or Gin, or on raw TCP

  • WebSocket Client

    ws:// and wss://.

  • TLS/SSL

    On both sides.

  • Subprotocols

    Offer, pick or require one, on either side.

  • HTTP Hijacking

    From http.Server or Gin.

  • Listener

    A read loop that validates against RFC 6455 and routes frames to your hooks.

  • Frame-level control

    Build and send your own frames when you need to.

  • Streaming

    Send or read a message larger than memory, frame by frame.

  • Compression

    permessage-deflate (RFC 7692), on both sides.

  • Memory in your hands

    Pick each connection's read and write buffer, as small as you need.

  • Memory protection

    Cap how much a peer can send, before and after decompressing.

  • Keepalive

    Ping on an interval, with a payload you choose per ping.

  • Concurrent sending

    Lock-guarded, and control frames are never stuck behind a long message.

  • And even more

    See the Guides →

Design concept

You control almost everything, from high level to low level.

wlgows never decides for you.

I believe development should be free, not locked down by the library. Developers should make their own tradeoffs.

Almost every function is a helper for one step of WebSocket. wlgows itself is built from these same helpers, at every level. So you can always do any step yourself, the same way wlgows does, and you always know what is going on.

  1. Keepalive pings
  2. Each message
  3. Each frame
  4. The handshake
  5. I/O buffers
  6. The raw connection

And even more. See the Guides →

Benchmarks

Compared with gorilla/websocket and gobwas/ws

0 allocs on every send
1.3x–3.2x faster large frame reads than gorilla
1.9x–2.8x faster small frame reads than gorilla

Client sends are slower, on purpose. wlgows uses a stronger masking key, and never writes to your buffer. Each faster path was measured and turned down, because correctness and safety come first.

Quick Start

A working echo server, and a client to talk to it.

main.go 
package main

import (
	"io"
	"log"
	"net/http"

	"github.com/weilun-shrimp/wlgows/v7"
)

// readMessage returns the bytes of one message. It decompresses a compressed
// message and checks text as UTF-8. See READING.md.
func readMessage(conn *wlgows.Conn, frames wlgows.DataFrames) ([]byte, error) {
	reader, err := conn.DataFramesReader(frames)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	defer reader.Close() // always close it
	return io.ReadAll(reader)
}

func main() {
	log.Fatal(http.ListenAndServe(":8001", http.HandlerFunc(handle)))
}

func handle(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	hijacker, ok := w.(http.Hijacker)
	if !ok {
		http.Error(w, "could not hijack connection", http.StatusInternalServerError)
		return
	}
	netConn, bufRW, err := hijacker.Hijack()
	if err != nil {
		http.Error(w, "could not hijack connection", http.StatusInternalServerError)
		return
	}
	defer netConn.Close()

	// Pass bufRW.Reader: net/http may have read the start of the first frame into it.
	conn, _, err := wlgows.ServerHandShake(netConn, bufRW.Reader, bufRW.Writer, r, wlgows.ServerHandShakeConfig{})
	if err != nil {
		return
	}

	// Ping, pong, close and reserved opcodes already answered.
	listener := conn.NewStandardListener()

	// SetConfig replaces all of it, so start from what the standard hooks left.
	config := listener.GetConfig()
	config.Text = func(frames wlgows.DataFrames) {
		message, err := readMessage(conn, frames)
		if err != nil {
			listener.PauseListen(err) // Listen returns err
			return
		}
		conn.SendText(message, wlgows.SendDataConfig{}) // echo
	}
	listener.SetConfig(config)

	log.Println("closing:", listener.Listen())
}

A short, runnable server. For production, follow the docs to pick your own limits and settings. The full server →

main.go 
package main

import (
	"bufio"
	"io"
	"log"

	"github.com/weilun-shrimp/wlgows/v7"
)

// readMessage returns the bytes of one message. It decompresses a compressed
// message and checks text as UTF-8. See READING.md.
func readMessage(conn *wlgows.Conn, frames wlgows.DataFrames) ([]byte, error) {
	reader, err := conn.DataFramesReader(frames)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	defer reader.Close() // always close it
	return io.ReadAll(reader)
}

func main() {
	// Dial only connects and builds the request. You run the handshake
	// yourself, so you can still add headers to `request` before it is sent.
	netConn, request, err := wlgows.Dial("ws://localhost:8001", nil)
	if err != nil {
		panic(err)
	}
	defer netConn.Close()

	// The reader and the writer take 4096 bytes/conn each; see READING.md and SENDING.md to shrink them.
	conn, _, err := wlgows.ClientHandShake(netConn, bufio.NewReader(netConn), bufio.NewWriter(netConn), request, wlgows.ClientHandShakeConfig{})
	if err != nil {
		panic(err)
	}

	listener := conn.NewStandardListener()

	config := listener.GetConfig() // what the standard hooks left
	config.Text = func(frames wlgows.DataFrames) {
		message, err := readMessage(conn, frames)
		if err != nil {
			listener.PauseListen(err) // Listen returns err
			return
		}
		log.Printf("received: %s", message)
	}
	listener.SetConfig(config)

	conn.SendText([]byte("Hello, WebSocket!"), wlgows.SendDataConfig{})

	log.Println("closing:", listener.Listen())
}
